# Preliminary results (generated by src/03_prelim_analysis.py)

## Sample
- pool: 7,583 videos, all in the random log; 7,551 of them appear in at least one standard log
- 7,035 of 7,583 videos kept (drop ads, posts without a video duration, < 50 random impressions); 6,043 creators
- random impressions per video: median 162; algorithmic impressions (same users, same period): median 9, zero for 11.6% of videos

## Quality measure reliability
- split-half Spearman 0.702; Spearman-Brown full-sample reliability 0.825
- top-quartile videos in half A that are also top-quartile in half B: 67.5% (chance 25%)

## R1. Exposure concentration
|                      |   Gini (videos) |   Top 1% share |   Top 10% share |   Gini (creators) |
|:---------------------|----------------:|---------------:|----------------:|------------------:|
| Random exposure      |           0.053 |          0.012 |           0.115 |             0.160 |
| Algorithmic exposure |           0.757 |          0.178 |           0.620 |             0.745 |

- algorithmic / random Gini across videos: 14.3 times

## R2. Does exposure follow quality?
- Spearman(quality, algorithmic exposure): shrunk long-view rate 0.4001; duration-adjusted percentile 0.3995
- Spearman(random long-view rate, algorithm-feed long-view rate), videos with >= 30 algorithmic impressions: 0.404 (quality measured under random exposure carries over to the real feed)

## R3. Hidden gems
Row = quality quartile, column = exposure quartile, cell = share of row (25% each if exposure ignored quality):

| q_quart   |   E1 low |    E2 |    E3 |   E4 high |
|:----------|---------:|------:|------:|----------:|
| Q1 low    |    39.8% | 31.5% | 20.5% |      8.2% |
| Q2        |    27.9% | 29.9% | 27.0% |     15.2% |
| Q3        |    19.2% | 24.9% | 29.0% |     26.9% |
| Q4 high   |    13.1% | 13.7% | 23.4% |     49.7% |

- Hidden gems (top-quartile quality, bottom-quartile exposure): 231 videos = 13.1% of high-quality videos; they received 0.06% of algorithmic impressions
- Over-exposed (bottom-quartile quality, top-quartile exposure): 144 videos, 4.5% of algorithmic impressions
- Hidden gems vs other high-quality videos: shrunk random long-view rate 0.156 vs 0.161; prior-period exposure (median) 15 vs 165
- Tie-breaking check: the E1 cut-off falls inside the tie at E = 2 (478 videos, 393 of them in E1). Gems with 200 random tie-breaks: mean 230.6, range 223-237; with a value threshold: 181 (E < 2) or 241 (E <= 2)

## R4. Path dependence: what predicts current exposure?
Standardized OLS, outcome = z(log(1 + current algorithmic exposure)); HC1 s.e. in parentheses; upload-type dummies included.

| Model                | Quality (random, duration-adj.)   | log prior exposure (previous 2 weeks)   | log duration   |    R² |
|:---------------------|:----------------------------------|:----------------------------------------|:---------------|------:|
| (1) quality only     | 0.409 (0.011)                     |                                         | -0.007 (0.014) | 0.178 |
| (2) + prior exposure | 0.101 (0.009)                     | 0.738 (0.009)                           | 0.019 (0.010)  | 0.622 |

- Spearman(quality, prior exposure) = 0.419: prior exposure partly reflects quality, so the coefficient in (2) is quality's association beyond prior exposure. Correlational, not causal.

## R5. Creator fairness of exposure (exposure share vs merit share)
Creators grouped by prior-period exposure quintile; exposure/merit = 1 means exposure proportional to merit (Singh & Joachims 2018).

| prior_q    |   creators |   exposure share |   merit share |   exposure / merit |
|:-----------|-----------:|-----------------:|--------------:|-------------------:|
| P1 lowest  |       1209 |            0.012 |         0.130 |              0.090 |
| P2         |       1208 |            0.038 |         0.151 |              0.249 |
| P3         |       1209 |            0.077 |         0.188 |              0.409 |
| P4         |       1208 |            0.182 |         0.224 |              0.812 |
| P5 highest |       1209 |            0.692 |         0.307 |              2.255 |

- Robustness, merit = sum of raw shrunk long-view rate: exposure/merit by group = 0.09, 0.25, 0.42, 0.83, 2.20
- 57.3% of creators receive less than half of their merit-proportional exposure; 9.3% receive none
- merit is a sum, so it scales with the number of videos: sample videos per creator mean 1.16, max 26; 86.9% of creators have one video. Grouping by prior exposure partly restates R4.
